From dd1311bcf0e62f0c515115f46a3813370f4a4bb1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andrzej Kacprowski <andrzej.kacprowski@linux.intel.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:58:42 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] accel/ivpu: Add bounds checks for firmware log indices

Add validation that read and write indices in the firmware log buffer
are within valid bounds (< data_size) before using them. If
out-of-bounds indices are encountered (from firmware), clamp them to
safe values instead of proceeding with invalid offsets.

This prevents potential out-of-bounds buffer access when firmware
supplies invalid log indices.

Fixes: 1fc1251149a7 ("accel/ivpu: Refactor functions in ivpu_fw_log.c")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v6.18+
Signed-off-by: Andrzej Kacprowski <andrzej.kacprowski@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Karol Wachowski <karol.wachowski@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Karol Wachowski <karol.wachowski@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260529115842.135378-1-andrzej.kacprowski@linux.intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_fw_log.c b/drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_fw_log.c
index 337c906b0210..275baf844b56 100644
--- a/drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_fw_log.c
+++ b/drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_fw_log.c
@@ -98,6 +98,11 @@ static void fw_log_print_buffer(struct vpu_tracing_buffer_header *log, const cha
 	u32 log_start = only_new_msgs ? READ_ONCE(log->read_index) : 0;
 	u32 log_end = READ_ONCE(log->write_index);
 
+	if (log_start >= data_size)
+		log_start = 0;
+	if (log_end > data_size)
+		log_end = data_size;
+
 	if (log->wrap_count == log->read_wrap_count) {
 		if (log_end <= log_start) {
 			drm_printf(p, "==== %s \"%s\" log empty ====\n", prefix, log->name);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modified Files

1. **drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_fw_log.c**
   - Added bounds validation for `log_start` and `log_end` indices obtained from the firmware log buffer.
   - Specifically:
     - If `log_start` is greater than or equal to `data_size`, it is clamped to `0`.
     - If `log_end` is greater than `data_size`, it is clamped to `data_size`.
   - These checks are inserted before the indices are used in the buffer access logic, preventing out-of-bounds reads when the firmware provides invalid index values.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications are confined to a single file and are directly related to each other: they both enforce safe bounds on indices derived from firmware data. The clamping of `log_start` and `log_end` ensures that subsequent buffer accesses (e.g., reading log messages) stay within allocated memory, eliminating a potential security or stability issue caused by corrupted or malicious firmware-supplied indices. The two checks are complementary—`log_start` is clamped from below to `0`, and `log_end` is clamped from above to `data_size`—and together they guarantee that the indices define a valid region within the buffer.
